issues.t: Frame rusting through
issues.sym: Flaking, swollen or holed frame rails, a sagging or loose rear bumper, a bed that shifts, or a failed safety inspection. Some owners found holes only when the truck was on a lift.
issues.why: The T100 frame has little rust protection, and in salted-road states it corrodes from the inside out. Dozens of owners told NHTSA their frames rotted through, sometimes near the spring mounts and control arms. Unlike the later Tacoma and Tundra, the T100 never got a frame recall.
issues.next: Have the whole frame inspected on a lift, tapping it with a hammer, especially near the rear spring hangers and front control arm mounts. If it is perforated, stop towing and hauling until a frame shop says it can be repaired safely.

issues.t: Steering relay rod can crack and break (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, a clunk when turning, or in the worst case the steering wheel spinning freely with no effect on the wheels.
issues.why: Turning the wheel hard at a standstill again and again can cause a fatigue crack in the steering relay rod (the center link). If it breaks, steering control is lost. Many owners also reported broken drag links and tie rods.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check your VIN for recall 05V389 (Toyota SSC 50N); the new relay rod is free. Have the rest of the steering linkage checked at the same time. If steering ever feels loose, stop and have it towed.

issues.t: Clutch pedal bracket cracks at the firewall
issues.sym: A snap or creak from the clutch pedal, a pedal that flexes, sits low or drops to the floor, and gears that are hard or impossible to select. Some trucks got stuck in gear.
issues.why: On manual-transmission T100s the clutch pedal bracket and the firewall around it can crack, or the bolt holding the pedal assembly can back out. The clutch then can't fully release. Toyota later fitted a redesigned bracket.
issues.next: If the pedal feels loose or flexes, have the bracket and firewall inspected before it breaks. A shop can fit the newer bracket and reinforce the firewall.

issues.t: Head gasket failure on the 3.4L V6
issues.sym: Coolant leaking onto the engine, a falling coolant level with no visible leak, overheating, white exhaust smoke or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Early 3.4L V6 engines had head gaskets that leaked. Toyota ran a special service campaign (X01) to replace cylinder head gaskets on some of these engines, and several 1996 T100 owners reported failures.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether campaign X01 was done on your VIN. If you are losing coolant or overheating, stop driving and have a cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test done.

issues.t: Rusted front lower control arm can break
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, then sudden collapse of one front corner. One owner's arm broke at highway speed, another's while backing out of a parking space.
issues.why: The front lower control arms rust through on trucks from salt-belt states, much like the frame they bolt to.
issues.next: Have the control arms and their frame mounts checked on a lift. Replace any arm with heavy rust scale or holes before it fails.

issues.t: Rusted brake and fuel lines leaking
issues.sym: Brake fluid or fuel dripping under the truck, a fuel smell, or a brake pedal that goes softer over time.
issues.why: The steel brake and fuel lines run along the frame and corrode along with it. Owners reported both brake fluid and fuel leaks from rotted lines.
issues.next: Do not drive with a fuel or brake fluid leak. Have the lines inspected on a lift and replace corroded sections.

issues.t: Seat belts won't retract or lock
issues.sym: The front seat belt hangs loose, gets shut in the door, or doesn't lock when you tug it.
issues.why: Weak retractor springs and worn retractors in the front belts are the cause. Many owners reported it, and dealers often couldn't reproduce it.
issues.next: A belt that doesn't lock won't protect you in a crash. Have the retractor replaced; a dealer can check for any Toyota coverage.

issues.t: Vibration at 35 to 60 mph
issues.sym: A shake through the truck or steering wheel that comes in around 35 mph and can be violent at highway speed, sometimes worse when speeding up or slowing down.
issues.why: Owners traced it to worn drive shaft universal joints, bent or out-of-round wheels, and in winter, ice packed inside the wheels.
issues.next: Have the wheels balanced and checked for runout, and the drive shaft U-joints inspected for play.

issues.t: Dealer-installed cruise control goes past set speed (recall)
issues.sym: With cruise set, the truck speeds up beyond the set speed or holds speed poorly on hills.
issues.why: Aftermarket cruise control units installed by Southeast Toyota and Gulf States Toyota dealers could fail to hold the set speed. Some owners with similar symptoms were told their VIN wasn't covered.
issues.next: Don't use the cruise control until it's checked. Ask a Toyota dealer whether recall 96E001 applies, and have the cruise unit disconnected if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Won't crank because of a worn starter
issues.sym: You turn the key and hear a click or nothing at all, often on and off at first.
issues.why: RepairPal lists a worn starter as the most common T100 problem. The starter contacts wear out with age.
issues.next: Have the battery and connections tested first. If they are fine, the starter usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifting poorly at high mileage
issues.sym: Harsh, late or slipping shifts, typically from 125,000 to 150,000 miles.
issues.why: RepairPal lists incorrect automatic shifting as a common T100 problem at higher mileage, usually from worn internal parts or old fluid.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. A fluid service may help if the fluid is only old; slipping usually needs a transmission shop.

issues.t: Truck can roll with the shifter in Park
issues.sym: The gear indicator doesn't match the gear selected, or the truck rolls after you put it in Park.
issues.why: Owners reported a shifter that could show the wrong gear and, in another case, a failed parking pawl that let the truck roll backward. A worn shift cable or linkage is a common reason the indicator and gear stop matching.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Have the shift cable, linkage and Park position checked right away.

issues.t: Driver's seatback breaks or drops backward
issues.sym: The driver's seatback suddenly gives way or reclines while driving.
issues.why: Owners reported the driver's seatback or recliner breaking, including one that caused a minor crash.
issues.next: If the seatback feels loose or the recliner slips, have the recliner mechanism and seat frame inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Blower motor wiring overheats and melts
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or smoke from under the dash, and the heater fan stopping or only working on some speeds.
issues.why: Owners of 1998 T100s reported melted fan connectors and a blower motor harness that shorted repeatedly and smoked.
issues.next: Turn the fan off and stop using it if you smell burning. Have the blower connector, harness and resistor replaced.

issues.t: Rear axle seal leaks oil onto the brakes
issues.sym: Oil on the inside of a rear wheel, weak or grabbing rear brakes, and a burning smell.
issues.why: Rear axle seals can leak gear oil onto the rear brake shoes, which then stop working properly.
issues.next: Get it fixed promptly. The axle seal must be replaced and any oil-soaked brake shoes replaced with it.

issues.t: Front brake caliper sticking
issues.sym: The truck pulls to one side, a wheel gets hot, a grinding or burning smell, and pads that wear out fast.
issues.why: One owner reported calipers locking up twice in 18 months. Rusted caliper slides or a sticking piston keep the pads dragging.
issues.next: Have the calipers, slides and brake hoses inspected, and replace any caliper that doesn't release.

issues.t: Hard brake pedal from vacuum or booster failure
issues.sym: The brake pedal becomes hard to push and the truck takes much longer to stop.
issues.why: An owner reported the vacuum brake system failing twice in two weeks. A leaking booster, vacuum hose or check valve takes away power assist.
issues.next: Do not drive until it's repaired. Have the vacuum hose, check valve and brake booster tested.

issues.t: Check engine light from EGR valve faults
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle or pinging, and a failed emissions test.
issues.why: An owner reported the EGR valve and its control switch failing, and Toyota issued parts information for EGR-equipped vehicles.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the EGR valve, vacuum switching valve and passages checked.

issues.t: Speedometer bounces or stops working
issues.sym: The speedometer needle jumps around, mostly under 50 mph, or drops to zero.
issues.why: Several 1997 owners reported a bouncing speedometer that came back even after the head and cable were replaced. The speed sensor or drive gear can also be at fault.
issues.next: Keep an eye on your speed with a phone app until fixed. Have the speed sensor, cable and drive gear checked together.

issues.t: Hazy, yellowed headlight lenses
issues.sym: Cloudy plastic headlight lenses and dim headlights at night.
issues.why: The plastic lenses oxidize from sunlight over time.
issues.next: Restore the lenses with a polishing kit or replace them, then have the headlight aim checked.
